A '''persona''' groups cards that represent the same person or thing in ''[[Star Wars CCG]]''. Under [[Players Committee]] rules, versions of a unique character, device, starship, vehicle or weapon can share a persona, including versions on different sides of the Force.<ref name="ar23">[[Media:SWCCG 2023 AdvancedRulebook.pdf|Star Wars CCG Advanced Rulebook]], Players Committee (2023), pp. 49–50 and 75. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261008192915id_/https://res.starwarsccg.org/rules/SWCCG_2023_AdvancedRulebook.pdf Internet Archive]. [[Players Committee Advanced Rulebook|Wiki transcription]].</ref>

'''List of personas:''' every persona with two or more cards has its own page, listed at [[:Category:Personas]].

== In play ==
Each player can normally have one version of a unique persona on the table. Both players can have their own version if the titles differ. A captive prevents Light from deploying that persona and Dark from deploying a captive of that persona. A stolen starship, vehicle, weapon or device prevents the other player from deploying that persona. Neither exception removes a version already legally on the table.<ref name="ar23" />

Cards that name a persona can generally refer to any version. For example, a reference to Luke can apply to [[Luke Skywalker]] or [[Commander Luke Skywalker]], and [[Chewbacca (persona)|Chewbacca]] and Chewie are interchangeable. A card that deploys on a named persona must still use the required card type.<ref name="gl20">[[Media:Decipher Glossary 1998.pdf|Star Wars Customizable Card Game Glossary, Version 2.0]], Decipher (November 1998), pp. 101 and 134–135. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20061215115652id_/http://decipher.com/starwars/rules/pdf/swccgglossary.pdf Internet Archive]. [[Decipher Glossary 2.0|Wiki transcription]].</ref><ref name="ar23" />

== Persona replacement ==
During the deploy phase, a player may replace one of their own unique characters with a different version of the same persona from hand. The new version needs at least the old character's power and ability and must fit the same pilot or passenger slot, if applicable. It must obey its own printed deployment restrictions. Other deployment restrictions apply except for location requirements such as presence and Force icons. The new version cannot carry a unique permanent weapon persona already on the table. Persona replacement has no Force cost and does not count as deployment.<ref name="ar23" />

Cards deployed on or targeting the old version transfer if they still apply. The other cards go to their owners' Lost Piles along with the replaced version.<ref name="ar23" />

== Decipher rules ==
[[Hoth Limited|Hoth]] introduced the persona rule with [[Commander Luke Skywalker]] and the original [[Luke Skywalker]] as examples of the same character.<ref name="hoth">[https://res.starwarsccg.org/rules/hothrules.pdf Star Wars CCG Hoth Rules Supplement], Decipher (1996), p. 7, “New Versions of Main Characters” and “Persona Rule”. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261021120454id_/https://res.starwarsccg.org/rules/hothrules.pdf Internet Archive].</ref> Decipher's 1998 Glossary allowed only one version of a unique persona on the table at a time. The Glossary used Vader as an example of the separate title limit. After one version returned to hand, the player could still deploy a differently titled Vader that turn.<ref name="gl20" />
